subject: Re: Acme Health — model fit & streaming follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-health.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health — model fit & streaming follow-up

Hi Samantha — great to meet today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Goal: Improve clinical note summarization quality in near-real-time while keeping per-request cost below your target. You mentioned a hard latency target for first token of ~250ms and that streaming partials should be coherent for your in-UI preview.
- Findings from the eval run we did on your sample corpus (attached): model quality varies with context-window and prompt formatting; some partial outputs show early divergence (incoherent mid-stream text) with the larger models on your truncated prompts.

What I attached:
- acme-eval-results-v1.csv — red/amber/green quality flags across sample prompts and models.
- prompt-set-v1.jsonl — the exact prompt permutations we ran (includes stop sequence examples).
- redwood-streaming-guidelines.pdf — recommended streaming params and patterns we use for similar customers.

Immediate recommendations (for a short proof-of-concept):
1) Evaluation: Please run the prompt-set-v1.jsonl through your integration with the redwood-7b-instruct and redwood-13b-instruct variants (we ran 7b/13b/70b in the attached). Focus on the 8k-context variants for your longer notes.
2) Streaming config: use explicit stop tokens in the prompt where possible (e.g., "### END_SUMMARY"), set a smaller stream_chunk_size (we recommend 256–512 bytes), and enable the coherent-prefix streaming_policy (see guidelines).
3) Latency levers: KV-cache warmup on repeated patient templates, and a small batching window (20–30ms) to improve throughput without hurting first-token SLO much.
4) Next call: I propose a 30-min follow-up on Thu to review the POC results and pick a production model. Please let me know availability.

I'll loop Jonas (our solutions lead) for the streaming/SRE details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme-eval-results-v1.csv, prompt-set-v1.jsonl, redwood-streaming-guidelines.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-health.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Health — model fit & streaming follow-up

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we set the POC in motion:

1) Partial output coherence: in our current prototype we see the model produce reasonable beginning tokens, then mid-stream it sometimes repeats or inserts unrelated phrases (more often on longer notes). Is that something you saw in the 13b vs 7b split? Any configuration knobs to reduce that behavior while keeping streaming?

2) Stop sequences: we do use a newline-based heuristic right now, but we saw some models ignore it mid-stream. Do we need to enforce an explicit token set or are there sampling settings that help?

3) Latency: our product team wants a first-token median below 250ms in prod (US-east). Your note about batching windows worries them — what tradeoffs should we expect?

If you can answer those, I can get Mike (engineering) to run the prompt set this week. Thu afternoon works for a follow-up.

—Samantha
Director, Product — Clinical Workflows
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-health.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health — model fit & streaming follow-up

Great questions — answered inline below. I've also flagged items for the POC checklist.

1) Partial output coherence (what we observed):
- In our eval CSV we marked several prompts where the 13b produced higher-quality final outputs but exhibited mid-stream repetition on very long contexts; the 7b-instruct had fewer mid-stream hallucinations on those exact truncated prompts but slightly lower final ROUGE/QA scores.
- Workarounds: use stronger stop tokens and prefix conditioning (e.g., add a short, high-confidence lead sentence in the prompt that anchors the model). The coherent-prefix streaming_policy helps by suppressing low-probability prefix edits.

2) Stop sequences and sampling knobs:
- Enforce explicit stop tokens in the prompt when possible (e.g., "### END_SUMMARY"). In addition set early_stop=true and provide stop=["### END_SUMMARY","

"].
- Reduce top_p to 0.92 and clip logits for special tokens to make stop enforcement stricter. If you need deterministic endings, we recommend switching to greedy decoding for the final 1–2 tokens (we can do a hybrid: streaming with sampling, final chunk with greedy).

3) Latency tradeoffs:
- Batching window: smaller windows (20–30ms) give better first-token latency but lower GPU utilization; larger windows (50–100ms) increase throughput but can push first-token median above your 250ms target in peak periods. For the POC we recommend targeting a 25ms batching window and a low-latency routing policy (route to dedicated pool in US-east).
- Other levers: model size (7b vs 13b) is the biggest single latency factor — 7b variants typically meet sub-200ms first-token easily in our US-east pools; 13b is borderline depending on sequence length. Quantized variants (q4) can help if you need quality closer to 13b at lower latency.

POC checklist (short):
- Run prompt-set-v1.jsonl against 7b-instruct and 13b-instruct (and 7b-q4 if you want a quantized baseline).
- Capture first-token latency distribution and stream chunk coherency cases (save transcripts).
- Try explicit stop tokens in 25% of prompts and hybrid final-token greedy in 25% to compare.

I'll attach the short config snippet we recommend in the POC. Happy to join the run with Mike if helpful.

Config snippet (example parameters):
- model: redwood-7b-instruct or redwood-7b-instruct-q4
- streaming_policy: coherent-prefix
- stream_chunk_size: 512
- batching_window_ms: 25
- stop: ["### END_SUMMARY","

"]
- early_stop: true
- top_p: 0.92

Best,
Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health — model fit & streaming follow-up

Adding a few SRE/ops notes from the eval CSV and our infra tests:

- Latency: on our US-east dedicated pools, redwood-7b-instruct median first-token is ~160–190ms with batching_window_ms=25 and stream_chunk_size=512 for 2k token contexts. 13b moves that to ~260–320ms depending on load.
- KV cache warmup: for repeated patient templates you can pre-warm the KV cache with a small synthetic request and keep a short-lived cache key per patient. This reduces tail latency for follow-on requests.
- Monitoring: emit per-request stream_chunk_timings and a coherence_score (we provide a lightweight function in the SDK). Create alerts when coherence_score drops >10% vs baseline.
- Fallbacks: configure a fast-fail fallback to a cheaper model (7b-q4) if first-token > 500ms or coherence_score < threshold. This keeps the UI responsive.

I'll open INF-1247 with a recommended observability dashboard and a starter alert set we use for similar accounts.

—Jordan (Infra)
